quest.title: The Roaming Abode
quest.description: At night, out in the wild, you encounter a little girl standing on a bamboo raft...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x35000

dialogues.text: Grandpa...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Hey there, kiddo, what are you doing out here at night? What's your name?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: I'm Xiangjun... I'm looking for my Grandpa... He was kidnapped by demons...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Demons? Here? What sort?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: I... I don't know either... Grandpa said that they're in the mountains, so I shouldn't run around by myself... But it's been three days now, and he still isn't back from the mountains...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's just trying to scare you, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks so too... Did he say what he was doing in those mountains?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: Grandpa's the village's herb gatherer. He found a divine plant recently, one that's said to only grow when watered with the blessed waters near Mt. Xuanlian.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: So... Might he have bumped into some kind of demon guarding the water?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry too much, Xiangjun. Your Grandpa might've just encountered some minor trouble. But it's also getting really late — mind if we send you home first?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: But I want to rescue him...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can help you.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! But if you don't go home, you might cause your Grandpa even more trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: Ah, I... don't want to do that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then let us look for him while you stay home, alright? Let's get you back to your home first.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: It's fine. I live in Qiaoying Village. I can head back myself.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: But... could you go look for Grandpa immediately? I'm worried about him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we'll be fine. That said... do you know where exactly he went?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: I only know that he went that way...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In that case, that's where we'll start.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangjun
dialogues.text: Thanks so much! I'll head back now. I won't cause you all any trouble... so I'll wait there for you!

talks.objective: Look for clues in the direction indicated by Xiangjun

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "I overslept! I have to get back before tomorrow, or no one's going to watch Xiangjun... Ah, I'm a fool...!"

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "If I remember right, there's a shortcut — a small road leading from Yaodie Valley to Mt. Xuanlian. Just need to get through that plus one mountain cave, and I should be golden..."

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "I've heard that there are monsters nearby, but I have to give this a shot..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This looks like something that her grandpa might've left behind. Seems like he took a small trail — let's go look for it as well!

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "...I was worried about monsters from the start, but..."

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "...So much... My thigh... Can't stop it..."

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "...So sleepy... But Mt. Xuanlian is just up ahead... Xiangjun, I'll definitely get those blessed waters..."

dialogues.speaker: Someone's Notes
dialogues.text: "Xiangjun... I'll surely get those blessed waters..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... He was attacked by monsters and was badly wounded in the process... Wait, and he still wants to get water from Mt. Xuanlian even so!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's hurry — Paimon hopes we can help him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. This should be the place, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why isn't anyone here? No trail to follow, either...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could he have gone back already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't think that would happen. He's been injured — could he have walked far?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But he's not around here either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could someone have met him on the road and rescued him? Paimon thinks that might have happened...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shall we go back to Qiaoying Village and ask around?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's get a bit of this "blessed water" first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, right. If Xiangjun's Grandpa was rescued, he might still need this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #In for a Mora, in for it all, eh? You're so thoughtful, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you, Traveler. You seem in a terrible hurry. Did some trouble come up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We... Well, do you know where Xiangjun and her grandfather live, Uncle Luo? We're looking for them.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Xiangjun? Never heard of her. Is she from around here? I'm sure I know everyone in the village...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? That can't be... We met a little girl outside who called herself Xiangjun, and said she lives in Qiaoying Village. She asked us to help her find her grandfather...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She also has a big bamboo raft!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Well, you can find those quite easily, but Xiangjun... I'm fairly sure there's no one by that name in our village. What does her grandfather go by?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's an herb gatherer.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: A herb gatherer? Let me think. We did have one, so I recall... But it's been three years since he passed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He passed away!?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Aye. He encountered monsters in the wild and... *sigh* Still, I doubt that's who you're looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: He was always a little off his rocker, and he never got married, never mind having descendants of any sort.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... What's going on here? So, that Xiangjun we met...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Could she have been the real demon!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What sorts of herbs did your herb gatherer, well, gather?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Flowers and grasses, none of which we've ever seen. 'Fraid I only know this and that about tea, so I'd be little help here...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: But I do remember that we found him near Mt. Xuanlian. He was still clutching a bottle of water.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: He said that he had a divine plant in his yard that needed that sort of blessed water to grow. Load of hogwash if you ask me — I mean, it's all just river water. Nothing special about it! Why'd he have to give up his life on account of something like that...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: *sigh* Still, after we buried him, we poured the water he obtained out in that yard of his. I hope that brought him some solace.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The blessed waters of Mt. Xuanlian? We went there and drew some water, too... So, this herb gatherer of yours...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think we're talking about the same person.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Well, that's strange happenings, and no mistake... Why don't you come with me? I'll take you to that fellow's yard.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: If you did draw water, I suppose you can just pour it out in his yard.

talks.objective: Go to the herb gatherer's house

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: If there's nothing else, I'll leave you to look around as much as you'd like.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So there really wasn't anyone named Xiangjun...?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: I'll ask around. Maybe it was just a little mistake somewhere. Y'know, like someone forgetting where they live, and such.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: In any case, thanks for helping that "adeptus" water the herbs. I'm sure he'll do what he can to defend you from harm as thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #This should be the right way, {NICKNAME}. Let's keep our eyes peeled.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? There's a campsite here. Could this have been where Xiangjun's grandfather stayed for a while?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Let's see if we can find any clues nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Blessed waters," Paimon's foot! These waters don't look special at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right. We forgot to ask Xiangjun where she lives in Qiaoying Village... Let's go back there and ask around!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Since we're already talking about it, I should probably add that we never really knew the name of that herb gatherer.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: He was an outsider, and we discovered that he was a bit... touched in the head the moment he arrived. He claimed that he'd picked divine herbs, but the pharmacy couldn't recognize them — much less buy them from him.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: But he had no other skills, and couldn't make the Mora needed to feed himself, so he had to knock on doors to ask for help. We took pity on him, and decided to feed him. His house was also built using Mora the villagers pooled together.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Later, some ignorant children would call him an "adeptus" on account of his mutterings about "divine herbs."

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Not the "Capital-A Adepti" who dwell in the clouds, I mean. Just an "adeptus" who could help protect the village from disaster.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: No one expected something that terrible to happen to him afterward, but once it did, everyone thought that this must've been him repaying us by protecting the village!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Everyone thanked him, and thus people have been reliably caring for his own home. We're almost there, by the way.
